disciplinary_grounds.description: Buying, selling, or fraudulently obtaining any optometry diploma, license, certificate, or registration
disciplinary_grounds.quote: buying, selling, or fraudulently obtaining, any optometry diploma, license, certificate, or registration

disciplinary_grounds.description: Selling or providing contact lenses or ophthalmic lenses inconsistently with statutory requirements or intentionally altering a prescription
disciplinary_grounds.quote: selling or providing contact lenses or ophthalmic lenses in a manner inconsistent with Section 58-16a-801 or intentionally altering a prescription unless the person selling or providing the lenses is a licensed optometrist or ophthalmologist

disciplinary_grounds.description: Representing oneself as or using the title of optometrist, optometric physician, doctor of optometry, or O.D. without a license
disciplinary_grounds.quote: representing oneself as or using the title of "optometrist," "optometric physician," "doctor of optometry," or "O.D.," unless currently licensed under this chapter

disciplinary_grounds.description: Using or employing the services of an optometric assistant in a manner not consistent with professional standards or applicable law
disciplinary_grounds.quote: using or employing the services of an optometric assistant to assist a licensee in any manner not in accordance with: (a) the generally recognized practices and standards of ethics of the profession; or (b) applicable state law or division rule

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failure to refer a patient to an appropriate licensed practitioner when the patient's condition does not respond to treatment or treatment is outside the licensee's scope
disciplinary_grounds.quote: failure to refer a patient to an appropriate licensed practitioner when: (a) the patient's condition does not respond to treatment; or (b) the treatment is not within the scope of competence or licensure of the licensee

disciplinary_grounds.description: Providing confidential patient information to third parties without a legal and professional basis
disciplinary_grounds.quote: providing confidential information regarding a patient to any third party who does not have a legal and professional ground for obtaining the information

disciplinary_grounds.description: Knowingly prescribing, selling, giving away, or administering prescription drugs not for a legitimate medical purpose, without proper diagnosis, or not in compliance with pharmacy law
disciplinary_grounds.quote: knowingly prescribing, selling, giving away, or administering any prescription drug unless: (a) for a legitimate medical purpose; (b) upon a proper diagnosis indicating the use of the drug in the amount prescribed or provided; and (c) in compliance with Section 58-17b-309

disciplinary_grounds.description: Giving or receiving fees, commissions, rebates, or other compensation for professional services not actually and personally rendered
disciplinary_grounds.quote: giving or receiving directly or indirectly any fee, commission, rebate, or other compensation for professional services not actually and personally rendered, except as part of a legal relationship within a lawful professional partnership, corporation, or association

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failure to transfer pertinent and necessary patient medical records to another optometrist or physician when requested by the patient
disciplinary_grounds.quote: failure to transfer pertinent and necessary information from a patient's medical records to another optometrist or physician when so requested by the patient or his representative, as designated in writing

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failure to provide a contact lens prescription to a person who sells contact lenses as required by statute
disciplinary_grounds.quote: failure to provide a contact lens prescription to a person who sells contact lenses in accordance with Section 58-16a-306

disciplinary_grounds.description: Falsely making an entry in or altering a medical record with intent to conceal wrongful conduct
disciplinary_grounds.quote: falsely making an entry in, or altering, a medical record with the intent to conceal: (a) a wrongful or negligent act or omission of an individual licensed under this chapter or an individual under the direction or control of an individual licensed under this chapter

disciplinary_grounds.description: Engaging in unprofessional conduct as defined in the general division act (Section 58-1-501)
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Grounds for refusal to issue a license to an applicant, for refusal to renew the license of a licensee, to revoke, suspend, restrict, or place on probation the license of a licensee, to issue a public or private reprimand to a licensee, and to issue cease and desist orders shall be in accordance with Section 58-1-401.
disciplinary_grounds.citation: Section 401 - Grounds for denial of license -- Disciplinary proceedings.

definition_quote.value: "Optometry" and "practice of optometry" mean any one or any combination of the following practices: (a) examination of the human eye and its adnexa to detect and diagnose defects or abnormal conditions; (b) determination or modification of the accommodative or refractive state of the human eye or its range or power of vision by administration and prescription of pharmaceutical agents or the use of diagnostic instruments; (c) prescription, ordering, administration, or adaptation of ophthalmic lenses, contact lenses, ophthalmic devices, pharmaceutical agents, laboratory tests, or ocular exercises to diagnose and treat diseases, defects, or other abnormal conditions of the human eye and its adnexa; (d) display of any advertisement, circular, sign, or device offering to: (i) examine the eyes; (ii) fit glasses or contact lenses; or (iii) adjust frames; (e) removal of a foreign body from the eye or its adnexa, that is not deeper than the anterior 1/2 of the cornea; and (f) consultation regarding the eye and its adnexa with other appropriate health care providers, including referral to other appropriate health care providers.
definition_quote.quote: "Optometry" and "practice of optometry" mean any one or any combination of the following practices

drug_authority.value: An optometrist may prescribe or administer pharmaceutical agents for the eye and its adnexa, including oral agents, subject to conditions: oral antibiotics only for eyelid-related or specified ocular conditions; hydrocodone combination drugs or Schedule III controlled substances only for pain of eye or adnexa, oral or topical, not exceeding 72-hour quantity, no refills. Schedule II controlled substances are prohibited except hydrocodone combination drugs if so scheduled and meeting conditions.
